newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt said still considering pension cuts.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt said still considering pension cuts.

text.p: The Italian government, despite opposition from the hard-left Communist Refoundation, is considering cutting health and pensions spending in the 1997 budget, the undersecretary of the public works ministry said.
Gianni Mattioli told reporters that cuts under examination would not touch the weakest parts of society.
"I think they're working on these re-touches (to the budget)," he said as he was leaving the prime minister's office.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi is due to meet his government allies, including Refoundation, shortly to discuss the budget which will be unveiled on Friday.

Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said earlier on Thursday that he had not dropped his opposition to pension cuts. "(The party) will not take a step forward or a step back," he told reporters. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
